approved: Social Services Legislation Amendment (Payments for Carers) Bill 2018
Written by a model from the explanatory memorandum; not the record
The bill would add an income test to the Carer Allowance payment and the associated health care card.
A family income threshold of $250,000 per year would determine eligibility for these payments, with those earning less continuing to qualify.
Savings from the test would fund a new Integrated Carer Support Service from September and October 2018.
Introduces an income test for Carer Allowance and its health care card.
Sets a family income limit of $250,000 per year for eligibility.
Directs projected savings to a new carer support service.
Carers who receive Carer Allowance or hold the Carer Allowance (child) Health Care Card.

The bill introduces an income test of $250,000 per year for carer allowance and the carer allowance (child) healthcare card from September 2018, affecting about one per cent of recipients, with savings redirected to an integrated carer support service; Labor supported the bill but expressed concern over the service's delayed implementation and lack of detail.

The government argued for introducing an income test of $250,000 per annum for carer allowance and the carer allowance (child) health care card from 20 September 2018, affecting around 6,500 recipients. The $85.6 million raised will fund a new integrated carer support service, including an expanded Carer Gateway website and regional delivery partners, to provide early-intervention and tailored services for carers.

The speaker supported the Social Services Legislation Amendment (Payments for Carers) Bill 2018, which introduces a $250,000 family income test for carer allowance and healthcare cards from 20 September 2018, arguing it will allow most carers to access better support if the government delivers on promises. The speaker criticised the government for delaying integrated carer support services from July to October 2018, and highlighted that Australia has nearly 2.7 million carers, including 15,000 in the Lindsay electorate, with unpaid care valued at $60.3 billion in 2015.

The member for Dobell supported the Social Services Legislation Amendment (Payments for Carers) Bill 2018, which introduces a family income test of $250,000 for the carer allowance and carer allowance child healthcare card from 20 September 2018. She argued that while Labor supports the change because savings will fund the Integrated Carer Support Service, the service is months behind schedule, and the government is failing carers by delaying support and mismanaging the NDIS and Centrelink.

The member supported the Social Services Legislation Amendment (Payments for Carers) Bill 2018, which introduces a $250,000 family income test for the carer allowance and carer allowance (child) healthcare card, but called on the government to deliver promised extra services for carers, citing delays in announcements.

The speaker opposed the Social Services Legislation Amendment (Payments for Carers) Bill 2018, which introduces a non-indexed $250,000 family income test for carer allowance, affecting 6,500 recipients in 2018-19, and argued the government delayed the Carer Gateway support services while prioritising tax cuts over carers.

The speaker argued that the Social Services Legislation Amendment (Payments for Carers) Bill 2018 should be supported but warned that Centrelink's 1,200 job cuts will worsen service delays, and cited families like Mia's with Dravet syndrome who sold their home due to high medical costs.

The bill introduces an income test for carer allowance from 20 September 2018, with a $250,000 threshold affecting only the 1% of recipients with family incomes above that level, and the $85.6 million in savings will fund new early intervention support services for carers.
